attributes.readMe:
# Person

## Summary
The one person base in the catalog: `name`, `email`, `phone`, `photo` (ImageSourceField) and computed `initials`/`title`, plus the avatar-row embedded view subclasses inherit. Extended by CRM `Contact` (which stores `firstName`/`lastName` and computes `name`), Service Desk `SupportAgent` and `SupportContact`, and HR `Employee` and `Candidate`. Rule: every person-shaped card in the catalog extends this; a subclass may redeclare a field with a narrower type (Contact's `phone` is `PhoneNumberField`) or compute `name` from its own parts.

## Import
```ts
import { PersonBase } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/people/person-base';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. As the shared identity base.** `Contact`, `SupportAgent`, `SupportContact`, `Employee` and `Candidate` all extend it,
which is exactly why `ApproveOfferCommand` can copy name/email/phone straight
across when a candidate is hired — the field names already match.

**2. As the initials source.** `initials` is computed, so avatars never render
blank even when no photo is set, and `title` falls back to a readable string
rather than an empty heading.

**3. As the photo holder.** `photo` is the catalog's **ImageSourceField**, not
a bare UrlField: it accepts either a pasted URL or a file uploaded into the
realm and exposes the winner as `photo.resolvedUrl`. Consumers read
`resolvedUrl`, never the raw inputs.

**4. As a base embedded row.** It defines an `embedded` format that subclasses
may override, so any person-shaped card gets a usable row for free.

## Template Usage
Embedded view renders photo (or initials fallback) + name + email.

Also exports `initialsOf(name)` — "Sofia Reyes" → "SR" — for any card that draws an avatar fallback.

**Non-goals:** direct instantiation — this is a shared base, not a standalone record; no addresses (unlike commerce Customer).
